text:
Maya (Support): Hey team, Zoe from FinPay reported a flood of 429s this morning starting ~08:21 UTC. They say it affected checkout flows for ~7m, ~20% of requests failed with 429. They included a sample: 

Zoe (Customer): We started seeing 429s at 08:21. No deploys on our side. We were doing normal traffic — around 1800 RPM overall for the app key. Response headers show `x-rate-limit-rpm: 1200` and `retry-after: 15` for many responses. Any immediate workarounds? :frowning:

Maya (Support): Thanks Zoe — forwarding to SRE/Eng to help triage. Do you have a request id from one of the 429 responses?

Zoe (Customer): Example request id: req_01GZ9Y7H3A2. Also attached a short pcap of the client bursts and a list of IPs. We have 6 backend workers hitting the Redwood API.

Ethan (SRE): Looking at platform metrics — there's a short regional surge in us-east-1 at 08:20:30. Per-key RPM for that app key spiked close to 3k for ~30s before decaying. Our global per-minute throttle for hosted tier is 1200 RPM and 10 TPM (example config for this customer was lower due to trial quota). The `x-rate-limit-rpm` header Maya mentioned matches that.

Priya (Eng): Can you paste the full headers from a 429? We need to confirm enforcement point (edge vs runtime). Also check whether they were hitting a per-account aggregate limit (requests coming from multiple app tokens) or a single token.

Maya (Support): Zoe confirmed single API key. Header dump: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:21:31 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 15
X-Rate-Limit-RPM: 1200
X-Rate-Limit-TPM: 60000
X-Request-Id: req_01GZ9Y7H3A2
{"error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "detail": "per-minute request limit exceeded"}
```

Ethan (SRE): That header set implies enforcement at the API gateway layer (edge). Edge maintains token->rpm counters and returns Retry-After. The spike to 3k RPM suggests a client-side burst rather than steady increase. Can you share client logs around 08:20?

Zoe (Customer): We found a cron misconfiguration. A nightly job that normally runs every 15m spawned 12 parallel workers after a failed retry loop. It resumed at 08:20 and all workers retried the same user queue causing a sudden spike. We're rolling a fix to add proper jitter/backoff.

Priya (Eng): That matches. Two recommendations for immediate mitigation: 1) Short-term: rotate API key so the in-flight retry flood fails fast on the client side (this is disruptive but quick). 2) Medium-term: we can request a temporary quota bump for this org while you fix the client behavior.

Maya (Support): Zoe — would you prefer we issue a temporary bump or want to rotate keys?

Zoe (Customer): Prefer temp bump if possible. Rotating keys would break other services this morning. How long does a bump take?

Ethan (SRE): We can provision a +2x RPM for 30 minutes manually from the console if you authorize it. That should cover the tail of the retry storm. We need a ticket and the org id.

Maya (Support): I created INC-20260310-1459 and requested org id and contact. Zoe, please confirm org id so I can escalate.

Zoe (Customer): Org id: org_fnp_82. Contact: zoe@finpay.co. Go ahead.

Priya (Eng): While SRE handles the bump, we'll add a temporary edge rule to smooth token counter resets: increase the sliding window dampening to reduce false positives for short bursts (non-ideal but buys a few extra seconds). Needs approval from infra lead.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260310-1459 assigned to SRE. Priority: P2.

Ethan (SRE): Bump applied: RPM -> 2400 for 45 minutes. Monitoring now. Edge rule tweak in progress (ETA 10m). Watch metrics for error rate.

Maya (Support): Zoe, can you confirm if 429s are dropping after the bump?

Zoe (Customer): Seeing immediate improvement. 429s dropped to <1% within 2m. Thanks all. We're pushing a client hotfix to add exponential backoff with jitter and cap concurrency to 4.

Priya (Eng): Action items for follow-up: 
- Customer to deploy client hotfix and confirm no more scheduled overlapping jobs. (Zoe)
- SRE to revert temporary edge dampening after 60 minutes and document the change. (Ethan)
- Support to capture exact request traces for three sample req ids and attach to INC. (Maya)
- Eng to review rate-limit UX for trial orgs — threshold too low for certain integration test patterns. (Priya)

Maya (Support): I'll attach req_01GZ9Y7H3A2, req_01GZ9Y7H3A3, req_01GZ9Y7H3A7 to the ticket with the client's pcap and a summary.

Ethan (SRE): Monitoring note: we saw a secondary small uptick in token contention around 08:50 when the client retries resumed after partial fix; still within bumped RPM. We'll keep an eye and let you know when we revert changes.

Zoe (Customer): Hotfix deployed 08:31. We limited concurrency and added exp backoff + jitter. No further 429s after 08:35. Appreciate the quick assist.

Priya (Eng): Postmortem checklist items suggested: 
- Document common client anti-patterns that cause short high-volume bursts (parallel retry storms, cron fan-out).
- Add a KB article for customers on how to interpret `x-rate-limit` headers and implement client-side backoff.
- Evaluate offering a soft-limit warning webhook for customers approaching RPM/TPM thresholds.

Maya (Support): Closing loop — Zoe: does this resolve the support ticket or do you want a follow-up call?

Zoe (Customer): All good. A short follow-up email with the list of changes would be helpful. Thanks :heart:

Maya (Support): Will do. Marking INC-20260310-1459 as mitigated; keeping open for postmortem doc.

Ethan (SRE): Reverting edge dampening at 09:15. No regressions noted.

Priya (Eng): I'll own the KB draft and ping product for the webhook feasibility study.

Maya (Support): Thanks everyone. Summary: client cron -> parallel retry storm -> exceeded per-key RPM -> edge returned 429 with Retry-After -> short-term RPM bump + edge tweak mitigated impact -> client hotfix rolled -> postmortem & KB to prevent recurrence.
